harmonicFunction: Slow 12/8 time (counted ONE-and-a, TWO-and-a, THREE-and-a, FOUR-and-a) gives every note immense breathing room and acoustic weight
Blending G minor pentatonic with G major pentatonic allows Stevie Ray to toggle between crying sorrow and sweet soul
Heavy .013-.058 string gauge tuned down a half-step produces massive acoustic mass, rich overtones, and thunderous low-end sustain
The dominant 9th chords (C9, D9) introduce jazz-blues sophistication over the raw Texas shuffle

techniques.name: Microtonal Vocal Bends & Heavy String Vibrato
techniques.description: Executing precise quarter-tone 'blues curls' and wide, singing wrist vibrato on heavy .013 gauge strings

notes: SRV used heavy strings (.013 to .058) tuned down a half-step for massive tone and string tension
Wide vibrato generated by rotating the entire forearm and wrist, not just the fingers
Microtonal bends (curling minor 3rd slightly sharp toward major 3rd) create a crying human vocal timbre
sequence: Strike 15th fret on high E string with heavy pick attack
Bend up a full step to G with index, middle, and ring fingers reinforcing the bend
Apply wide, pulsating circular vibrato at the peak of the bend
tips: Reinforce bending fingers with two fingers behind for pitch control on heavy strings
Let the pick dig deep into the string to produce that distinctive woody SRV 'pop'

techniques.name: Texas Slow Blues Comping & Chord-Melody
techniques.description: Blending stinging lead fills seamlessly into punchy dominant 9th chord stabs

notes: Seamless integration of rhythm and lead playing pioneered by Jimi Hendrix and Albert King
Stab movable C9 and D9 chord grips on offbeats between vocal lines
Use thumb-over neck grips to fret root bass notes while pinky executes high fills
sequence: Lead phrase in G minor blues box at 15th fret
Stab C9 chord (X-3-2-3-3-3) with aggressive pick rake
tips: Keep picking wrist dynamic and bouncy to match Chris Layton's snare rimshots
Roll off guitar tone knob slightly (to 7) to eliminate harsh ice-pick treble

sections.name: Opening Slow Blues Masterclass (Solo 1)
sections.technique: Microtonal Vocal Bends & Heavy String Vibrato
sections.description: The jaw-dropping opening guitar solo that announced Stevie Ray Vaughan to the world, packed with passion and fire.
notes: Recorded live in one single take at Jackson Browne's studio in Los Angeles
Full-step and 1.5-step bends executed with immense finger strength
Rake across muted lower strings into stinging treble target notes

sections.name: Verse 1 Vocal Narrative & 9th Chord Comping
sections.description: Soulful vocal delivery followed immediately by crying guitar answers between each lyric line.
sections.progression: I7 - IV9 - I7 - V9 - IV9 - I7
notes: Leave dynamic space during vocal lines
Answer each vocal phrase with an expressive blues lick
Smooth sliding into 9th-chord voicings

sections.name: Chromatic Descending Turnaround
sections.description: Stevie's signature chromatic descending bass walkdown setting up the turnaround to D9.
notes: Fret the walking bassline on the D and A strings while holding upper notes
Accent the crunch of the Eb diminished passing note
Slam the D9 dominant chord with authority

sections.name: Main Extended Solo (Part 1 - Dynamic Whisper to Burn)
sections.technique: Microtonal Vocal Bends & Heavy String Vibrato
sections.description: The opening chorus of the main solo starting with delicate, singing 15th-position phrases that swell in intensity.
notes: Roll Stratocaster volume knob to 6-7 to create warm, woody clean bite
Curl the minor third (Bb) microtonally toward the major third (B)
Use deep, circular wrist vibrato that sustains across beats

sections.name: Main Extended Solo (Part 2 - Triplet Fury & Double Stops)
sections.technique: Microtonal Vocal Bends & Heavy String Vibrato
sections.description: High-energy triplet double stops on the B and high E strings driving the amplifier into roaring natural compression.
notes: Ibanez Tube Screamer engaged for high-mid singing boost
Strike double stops on strings 1 and 2 with an aggressive downward pick rake
Lock into Layton's rolling snare shuffle

sections.name: Outro Solo & Tremolo-Picked Cadence
sections.technique: Microtonal Vocal Bends & Heavy String Vibrato
sections.description: Tremolo picking and screaming bent vibrato carrying the track to its explosive conclusion.
notes: Rapid 16th-note tremolo picking on the high G note at fret 15
Wide pitch bends on the 18th fret pushing the Stratocaster neck
Final raked G7 power chord sustaining into amplifier decay

beginner.title: Slow 12-Bar Blues Form & 9th Chords
steps: Tune down half-step to Eb Standard (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)
Master the 12-bar blues form in G (G7, C9, D9)
Count slow 12/8 time (ONE-and-a, TWO-and-a, THREE-and-a, FOUR-and-a)

intermediate.title: Minor/Major Blues Mixing & Call-and-Response
steps: Practice combining G minor pentatonic and G major pentatonic
Learn the classic SRV opening slow-blues lick

advanced.title: Vocal Microtonal Bends & Extended Soloing
steps: Master wide, circular wrist vibrato on sustained notes
Execute quarter-tone microtonal vocal curls on the 3rd and 7th degrees
Build hand strength to play through the 5-minute extended solo with dynamic authority

commonMistakes: Over-bending or under-bending slow blues notes—pitch accuracy must be surgically precise
Rushing through the 12/8 compound meter instead of letting notes hang and breathe
Using a thin pick or light attack, resulting in an anemic tone lacking the woody SRV snap
practiceRoutine: 5 min: Finger warm-up and bending pitch calibration with tuner
10 min: Slow wrist vibrato practice on sustained whole notes
15 min: Call-and-response phrasing drills over a slow 12-bar backing track at 60 BPM
10 min: Extended solo dynamics practice: building from whisper to roar
focusAreas: Microtonal pitch intonation and emotional bend contour
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 60 BPM in 12/8 time (or 4 heavy beats with triplet subdivisions)
Practice landing notes slightly behind the beat for an authentic Texas slow-drag feel
Let silence work as a musical instrument between phrases
